title: Model pipeline fit and benchmark prioritization demo
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Nimbus Retail through the model catalog and how benchmarks feed prioritization heuristics. Discussion focused on runtime compatibility matrices, kernel mapping for quantized models, and explicit bench criteria for pilot. Nimbus asked about SOC2/KMS, private deployment options, and cost sensitivity for 100 qps inference. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a focused bench for two candidate models and share cost/latency projections plus security docs.
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send sandbox benchmark plan + spreadsheet - 2026-06-06
Priya Rao - Prepare short runbook on kernel/quantization compatibility and console screenshots - 2026-06-08
Evan Carter - Provide sample request distribution and 90th percentile latency SLAs - 2026-06-07
Marisol Vega - Share network topology (VPC peering details) for pilot - 2026-06-09
next_steps: Redwood to run 48–72h bench on two shortlisted open models and return cost/latency tradeoff sheet
Schedule a pilot kickoff (2 week) pending bench results
Share SOC2 + KMS integration docs and pilot deployment checklist
questions: What quantization levels do you support out-of-the-box?
How does routing handle model variants when a node is saturated?
Can we get tenant-level audit logs and KMS integration for Private?
What's the expected unit token cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Marcus from product. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Evan Carter: Good thanks, Evan here. We just finished a sprint so this timing is good.
[00:10] Marisol Vega: Marisol, hi. We'll be looking at how the catalog maps to our infra.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Awesome, quick agenda — demo the catalog selection flow, show benchmark signals we surface, and then dive into compatibility matrix (kernel/hw) and routing policies. We'll leave time for your questions and pilot scoping.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: Also want to make sure we cover cost/latency tradeoffs because I know Nimbus has a sensitivity there — you mentioned 100 qps in the notes?
[00:31] Evan Carter: Yes 80–120 qps during peak testing, with 95th latency ideally under 200ms for short prompts. If that's not possible we can accept 300ms but cost needs to scale down.
[00:41] Priya Rao: Got it. When we look at the catalog we rank models by bench score, cost per token estimate, and runtime fit. I'll share the scoring rubric in the deck.
[00:49] [00:49] (screen share starts) Priya Rao: Here is the model catalog — on the left you can filter by architecture, quantization support, and hardware compatibility. Notice these two models we highlighted — both open source, one is a 7B dense FP16 variant, the other is a 6.9B with 4-bit quantized weights.
[01:05] Marisol Vega: Quick question — our infra is on GCP with a mix of A10 and H100s; does the catalog show kernel-level compatibility?
[01:12] Priya Rao: Yes, we surface a compatibility matrix: kernel mapping for that model family, preferred kernels for H100 vs A10, and an estimated performance multiplier. There can be transcription noise here — sometimes the kernel name is mis-typed in the UI, so we highlight recommended kernel version e.g., cuBLAS-rtX or our tuned nv-accel kernel.
[01:28] Evan Carter: And quantization — if we pick the 4-bit variant what's the expected accuracy drop?
[01:33] Priya Rao: We attach bench deltas; for conversational benchmarks we saw ~1–2% drop in helix bench score for many tasks, but the cost per token reduces by 30–40% on NVIDA Ampere gen. We'll attach exact bench run links.
[01:44] [01:44] Speaker 2: sorry — there was a lag.
[01:47] Jordan Lee: No worries, go ahead Samir.
[01:49] Samir Patel: Samir here. Curious how routing policies work — if the preferred model is saturated do requests fallback to a cheaper variant automatically?
[01:56] Priya Rao: Yes, we have smart routing. You can define a policy: prefer low-latency model, fallback to cost-optimized model, and route by region or tenancy. We also support automatic variant downgrade when latency SLO is violated, with circuit breaker thresholds.
[02:09] Marisol Vega: Does that keep user response semantics consistent? I'm worried about hallucination/regression when switching models mid-conversation.
[02:16] Priya Rao: Great point. We recommend sticky routing for session-based flows or KV/prefix cache warming when switching. Redwood's console surfaces regressions and you can set guardrails — e.g., run a head-to-head eval on a canonical prompt set to detect semantic drift before auto-fallback.
[02:31] Evan Carter: That helps. On security we need SOC2 and KMS, and for pilot we may want a Private deployment inside our VPC.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: We support Private with customer-managed KMS and can offer audit logs per tenant. We'll send SOC2 artifacts and our KMS integration guide. There's also an on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
[02:49] Tina Huang: For network, do you require VPC peering or can we use a transit gateway / proxy?
[02:56] Priya Rao: We can work with peering or a proxy setup; for the pilot we usually do VPC peering for simplicity, but we've integrated via VPN/transit as well. We'll include a checklist in the runbook.
[03:07] [03:07] (screen clicks) Priya Rao: Back to the bench signals — our catalog exposes multiple signals: throughput (tokens/s), latency percentiles, bench score (task-level), memory footprint, and kernel affinity. You can weight signals in the Optimize product to produce a ranked shortlist.
[03:23] Marisol Vega: How do we bring our own bench data? We have internal prompts and customer dialogs.
[03:28] Priya Rao: You can upload a suite of prompts into Optimize; we run bench jobs against candidate models and produce a comparison sheet. We can plug your request distribution so the cost model is realistic (prefix lengths, tokenization).
[03:39] Jordan Lee: For Nimbus I'd recommend a two-model shortlist for the pilot — a higher-accuracy FP16 model and a cost-optimized quantized model. We'll run a 48–72 hour bench against your sample distribution.
[03:49] Evan Carter: What's the unit token cost delta hosted vs dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine.
[03:54] Jordan Lee: Ballpark — hosted API for those models might be 0.0009–0.0012 per token for the FP16 family, while dedicated/reserved can drop that by 30–50% depending on utilization and batch profiles. We'll give a precise sim in the bench spreadsheet.
[04:08] Samir Patel: Is pre-warming and KV cache accounted for in those numbers?
[04:12] Priya Rao: We model prefix caching separately. If you have strong cache locality, effective token cost can drop significantly; Optimize will surface a projected cost curve given cache hit rates.
[04:21] [04:21] Speaker 1: (laughs) there's a lot of knobs.
[04:25] Priya Rao: Totally — that's why we produce recommended profiles per route so you don't have to tune everything manually.
[04:30] Jordan Lee: Quick detour — any constraints from procurement/security folks we should know?
[04:35] Samir Patel: We need a standard DPA, a security questionnaire answer, and proof of SOC2. Also looking at data residency — some PII workflows must stay in EU.
[04:44] Jordan Lee: We have DPA templates and SOC2 coverage — will share. For residency we can pin routes to EU regions and run Private if needed.
[04:51] Evan Carter: For the pilot what metrics would you track to recommend production rollout?
[04:56] Priya Rao: Typical set: 95th/99th latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, regression rate on canonical eval set, and error/retry counts. We'll instrument with tracing hooks for per-request model attribution.
[05:09] Marisol Vega: Do you expose token-level cost breakdown in the console?
[05:12] Marcus Chen: Yes, the Console shows token breakdown by prompt vs completion, per-route and per-model, and you can export CSV. Also rollouts and canary controls are available for A/B.
[05:22] Evan Carter: Good. For the bench run, we'll share our sample payloads and tokenization profiles.
[05:27] Jordan Lee: Perfect — we'll use those as bench inputs. I'll outline the bench plan: 48–72h runs for both models with your distribution, capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput at 100 qps, and cost simulation at observed batch sizes.
[05:41] Tina Huang: On infra — if we want to test dedicated capacity, how long to provision?
[05:47] Jordan Lee: For dedicated reserved we can provision a short-term pool for pilot in days if capacity exists in the region, otherwise up to two weeks for commitments. For speed we often do hosted with capacity reservation for the pilot.
[05:58] Priya Rao: I'll also prepare a short doc on kernel mapping — for quantized models we prefer certain kernels, and we'll note any workarounds for A10.
[06:08] Marisol Vega: That will be helpful. Also want to confirm the console can surface the compatibility matrix per model version.
[06:14] Priya Rao: Yes, each model page shows supported kernels, tested sequence lengths, and known caveats — e.g., model X has kv-cache fragmentation at >4k tokens on some kernels.
[06:25] Evan Carter: Any limitations around function calling / tooling when you change model variants? We depend on structured outputs.
[06:30] Priya Rao: Structured outputs are supported but you should lock in the model family for tool-heavy flows or add a validation step when fallback happens. We can also pin function schemas and run a sanity eval on fallback candidates.
[06:43] [06:43] (brief pause) Jordan Lee: Ok, let's recap and get to action items. We'll run that bench on two shortlisted models once Nimbus uploads the request distribution. We'll share SOC2/KMS docs and a kernel compatibility runbook. Pilot kickoff to follow bench.
[06:58] Evan Carter: Sounds good. One last item — can Priya share a short video clip of the console flow for our internal docs?
[07:04] Priya Rao: Absolutely, I'll record a 3–4 minute clip and attach console screenshots.
[07:09] Marisol Vega: Thanks, appreciate it.
[07:11] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD with the bench plan and calendar invite for pilot kickoff tentative.
[07:18] Samir Patel: Thanks, bye.
[07:20] [END]
